_comment: One session on the wire, exactly as the client posts it to POST /v1/sessions/summarize.
Read by both ends of the request, and by neither's production code. The client's DraftSender
writes this shape; the backend's SummarizeBundle reads it. Nothing else binds them: the backend
must not depend on a Windows-only client, so the field names ARE the contract, and a contract
that lives only in two comments is a contract that drifts.
It drifted before anyone could notice, because until 2026-09-22 nothing had ever sent a bundle.
The client's own SessionBundle carries `image` as a PATH -- frames/f-0002.jpg -- because that is
what a session looks like on disk, and the backend has always wanted base64 bytes under the same
name. Two readings of one field name, and no test could see it while the sender was a stub.
Change this file only when both sides change with it. ClientWritesTheContract (client) and
TheContractIsWhatThisEndpointAccepts (backend) are the pair that notice.
The image is eight bytes of JPEG header rather than a real screenshot: what is under test is the
shape of the request, and a fixture nobody can read is a fixture nobody can check.
